intro_script: Welcome to your daily research news digest for November 23, 2026. Today we cover AI team dynamics, LLM calibration, and effective machine learning rollouts. Tune in for the details.
outro_script: And that's all for your research roundup of November 23rd, 2026. Remember, more agents mean brighter ideas! Thanks for diving into the deep end with us. Until next time, keep questioning!

items.title: Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams
items.summary: The study investigated how the number and formation of AI agents affect productivity and diversity in human-AI brainstorming teams. Experiments compared teams with one versus two AI partners against human-human dyads. With one AI partner, humans paired with an average-calibrated AI generated more ideas, while with two partners, this effect disappeared. AI presence increased the global diversity of human-authored ideas, but a second AI was necessary for increased within-session differentiation. Ultimately, the number and formation of AI partners significantly reshape human contributions to the brainstorming process.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Adding One More Agent: How AI Team Size and Formation Shape Productivity and Diversity in Human-AI Brainstorming Teams" investigates how the number and formation of AI agents affect productivity and diversity in human-AI brainstorming teams, finding that the optimal number of AI partners depends on the desired outcome. The study compared teams with one versus two AI partners against human-human dyads. Experiments revealed that when humans paired with a single AI partner, the team generated more ideas, whereas the effect of the single AI partner diminished when two partners were introduced. Furthermore, the presence of AI increased the global diversity of human-authored ideas, but a second AI was necessary to increase within-session differentiation. Ultimately, the number and formation of AI partners significantly reshape human contributions to the brainstorming process. This research indicates that the configuration of human-AI collaboration directly influences the quality and variety of creative output in team settings.

items.title: Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs
items.summary: Large language models require benchmarking to assess whether they exhibit normative-descriptive calibration. This involves testing if a model treats matched candidates differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one. The study introduces the Normative-Descriptive Calibration Benchmark (NDCB) to measure this calibration across different LLMs. Results show that some models, like Claude Sonnet and Opus, strongly separate these framings, while others, like GPT-5.5, show negative calibration. Separating disparities and prescribing them are distinct behaviors that vary across different language models.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Beyond Demographic Discrimination: Benchmarking Normative-Descriptive Calibration in LLMs" details a study benchmarking Large Language Models on normative-descriptive calibration. The research assesses whether models treat matched candidates differently when asked to describe an outcome versus decide one, revealing varying calibration behaviors across different models. The study introduced the Normative-Descriptive Calibration Benchmark to measure this calibration across various Large Language Models. Results indicated that some models, including Claude Sonnet and Opus, strongly separate these framings, while others, such as GPT-5.5, exhibited negative calibration. This demonstrates that the separation of disparities and the prescription of those disparities are behaviors that vary depending on the specific language model architecture. This research provides a framework for evaluating the internal consistency of LLM reasoning processes. Further investigation into these calibration metrics is warranted for the development of more aligned artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: Don't Discard Your Rollouts: Reusing Teacher RL Traces for Student Distillation
items.summary: Reusing teacher Reinforcement Learning (RL) rollouts can be a viable method for student distillation, addressing the computational expense of methods like PPO and GRPO. Naive approaches using rollouts perform worse than canonical distillation or are unstable for DPO methods. The authors propose treating rollout reuse as a data selection problem using metadata from GRPO to select student-compatible completions. This involves ordering data using prompt pass rates and using teacher log-likelihoods as a proxy for selection. The resulting two-stage recipe achieves performance comparable to canonical distillation across reasoning and coding tasks without extra inference costs.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Don't Discard Your Rollouts: Reusing Teacher RL Traces for Student Distillation" details a method for reusing teacher Reinforcement Learning rollouts to distill knowledge to students, achieving performance comparable to canonical distillation without additional inference costs. The research proposes treating rollout reuse as a data selection problem by utilizing metadata from GRPO to select student-compatible completions. This involves ordering the data based on prompt pass rates and employing teacher log-likelihoods as a proxy for selection. This two-stage recipe successfully achieves performance equivalent to canonical distillation across reasoning and coding tasks. This development suggests a pathway to more computationally efficient methods for knowledge transfer in reinforcement learning models.

items.title: LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Asynchronous, Federated Fine-Tuning
items.summary: Federated fine-tuning with low-rank adapters often uses averaging, which is problematic in asynchronous settings with heterogeneous data. LEAN proposes library-based adaptation to replace averaging by maintaining a library of rank-1 basis pairs. Participants check out, locally fine-tune, and check back in these adapters, shuffling them across sites for exposure to diverse data. This method operates asynchronously and communicates only low-rank parameters, avoiding aggregation. LEAN significantly outperforms averaging baselines across benchmarks while handling data heterogeneity and asynchrony effectively.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "LEAN: Library-Based Adaptation for Asynchronous, Federated Fine-Tuning" reports a method for federated fine-tuning that utilizes a library-based adaptation technique to replace averaging. The research demonstrates that this approach significantly outperforms averaging baselines when handling data heterogeneity and asynchrony in distributed settings. Participants check out, locally fine-tune, and check back in low-rank adapters, which are then shuffled across sites for exposure to diverse data. This method operates asynchronously and communicates only the low-rank parameters, thereby avoiding explicit aggregation of model weights across the network. The process maintains a library of rank-one basis pairs rather than relying on averaging of fine-tuned weights. This technique effectively manages the challenges inherent in asynchronous and heterogeneous federated learning environments. The findings suggest a pathway for more robust and effective decentralized model training across diverse data sources.

items.title: Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs
items.summary: The method proposes a communication-efficient, non-iterative federated spectral approach for learning shared latent representations from multi-institutional Electronic Health Record (EHR) data. Institutions share aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary instead of patient-level records to preserve privacy and reduce communication costs. A central server aggregates these summaries to recover the shared low-rank structure and the direction for interpretable representation recovery. Simulations demonstrate that the method accurately estimates latent components and outperforms existing benchmarks when applied to stroke patient data. This approach aims to uncover clinically meaningful, subgroup-specific patient representations across different healthcare facilities.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - stat.ML, "Communication-Efficient Federated Learning of Latent Patient Representations from Multi-Institutional EHRs" details a method for learning shared latent representations from multi-institutional Electronic Health Record data through communication-efficient federated learning. The approach utilizes a non-iterative federated spectral method where institutions share only aggregate marginal frequencies and a low-rank spectral summary instead of patient-level records to ensure privacy and minimize communication overhead. A central server aggregates these summaries to reconstruct the shared low-rank structure and the direction necessary for recovering interpretable representations. Simulations indicate that this methodology accurately estimates latent components and achieves superior performance compared to existing benchmarks when applied to stroke patient data. This work suggests a pathway for discovering clinically meaningful, subgroup-specific patient representations across disparate healthcare facilities. Future research will focus on the scalability of this approach in larger, more complex medical datasets.

items.title: Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis
items.summary: The research analyzes partial-edit deepfake localization using an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization (SAL). The study evaluates localization performance across different editing conditions, categorized by content, meaning change, and editing operation. Findings indicate that localization is weaker on the SSR-Speech subset, and deletions pose the most challenging editing operation for both representations. Single aggregate scores mask these specific weaknesses, suggesting separate evaluation across generators and edit types is necessary. Ultimately, the work emphasizes the need for finer-grained analysis of partial-edit localization performance.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Towards Robust Partial-Edit Deepfake Localization: An edit and Generator Conditioned Analysis" analyzes partial-edit deepfake localization using an edit- and generator-conditioned analysis of Segment-Aware Localization. The research evaluated localization performance across different editing conditions categorized by content, meaning change, and editing operation. The study found that localization performance is weaker on the SSR-Speech subset, and deletions represent the most challenging editing operation for both representations. Single aggregate scores obscure these specific weaknesses, indicating that separate evaluation across generators and edit types is necessary for accurate assessment. The work stresses the requirement for finer-grained analysis of partial-edit localization performance. This research points toward the necessity for more detailed methods in assessing the robustness of deepfake localization techniques.

items.title: AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress
items.summary: AstronautBench measures agent self-improvement across episodes by assessing knowledge, evidence, and progress in an embodied world. It uses the game Outer Wilds structure where knowledge persists across episode resets, focusing on what the agent knows, what evidence supports that knowledge, and how far it advances. The benchmark involves measuring reached locations, revealed facts, and the correctness of answers to world knowledge questions. Evaluations using different LLM judges show that these three measures do not align, providing a complete picture of self-improvement. For example, correctness increases, but the support from evidence does not always follow, revealing limitations in simple progress tracking.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "AstronautBench: Measuring Agent Self-Improvement Across Episodes Through Knowledge, Evidence, and Progress" details a benchmark for assessing agent self-improvement across episodes by measuring knowledge, evidence, and progress in an embodied world. The benchmark utilizes the game Outer Wilds structure where knowledge persists across episode resets, focusing on what the agent knows, the evidence supporting that knowledge, and the agent's advancement. Evaluations assessed reached locations, revealed facts, and the accuracy of answers to world knowledge questions. Studies using different large language model judges indicated that these three metrics do not consistently align, demonstrating that correctness may increase without a corresponding alignment in the support from evidence, revealing limitations in simple progress tracking methodologies. This work provides a framework for more nuanced evaluation of autonomous agent development in complex environments.

items.title: Graph-XGB: A Hybrid GNN Framework for Outdoor-to-Indoor 5G Signal Reconstruction via Aerial-Only UAV RF Sensing
items.summary: Graph-XGB is a hybrid Graph Neural Network (GNN) framework designed to reconstruct indoor 5G signals from aerial-only Radio Frequency (RF) sensing data. It employs a modified SpiderGNN encoder on a graph incorporating a Floor-Aware 3D Distance metric to process UAV boundary measurements. This process maps the measurements into a 10-dimensional manifold using PCA, which is then fused with spatial features for prediction. Independent, physics-tailored XGBoost regressors are used to decode these embeddings, effectively decoupling path-loss and interference-dependent modeling. Evaluation on a real-world dataset showed Graph-XGB achieved the highest accuracy for RSSI and RSRP reconstruction compared to other architectures.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Graph-XGB: A Hybrid GNN Framework for Outdoor-to-Indoor 5G Signal Reconstruction via Aerial-Only UAV RF Sensing" details a novel framework for reconstructing indoor 5G signals using only aerial Radio Frequency sensing data, achieving the highest accuracy for RSSI and RSRP reconstruction. The research introduces Graph-XGB, a hybrid Graph Neural Network framework that utilizes a modified SpiderGNN encoder incorporating a Floor-Aware 3D Distance metric to process UAV boundary measurements. These measurements are mapped into a ten-dimensional manifold using Principal Component Analysis, which is subsequently fused with spatial features for prediction. Independent, physics-tailored XGBoost regressors are employed to decode these embeddings, effectively separating the modeling of path-loss and interference dependencies. Evaluation on real-world data demonstrated that Graph-XGB outperformed other architectures in reconstructing these 5G signal metrics. This advancement suggests significant potential for deploying accurate indoor signal mapping using remote sensing techniques.

items.title: Who Should Verify? Reviewer Selection with Partial Information and Outcome Audits
items.summary: Selecting an AI reviewer requires evidence of their performance after reading a draft. The research investigates the cost of certifying procedures that achieve a specified number of correct answers relative to the best procedure. The work develops algorithms to find the cheapest certificate in hindsight when reviews and answer keys have associated prices. Experiments show that a targeted audit of review keys reduced the number of keys needed on certain datasets without sacrificing accuracy on others. The findings suggest methods for optimally selecting and auditing reviewers in machine learning contexts.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.LG, "Who Should Verify? Reviewer Selection with Partial Information and Outcome Audits" investigates the cost associated with certifying procedures for selecting AI reviewers based on performance. The research develops algorithms to identify the least costly certification method in hindsight when review data and answer keys have associated costs. Experiments demonstrated that a targeted audit of review keys successfully reduced the number of keys required on specific datasets without compromising accuracy on others. This work proposes methods for optimizing the selection and auditing of reviewers within machine learning environments. The findings offer a framework for more efficient and verifiable systems in the development of artificial intelligence.

items.title: Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers
items.summary: LLM theorem solvers vary in proving ability and inference cost, leading to inefficient computation when not managed properly. BudgetPV is an agentic system that allocates computation across subgoals and heterogeneous LLM solvers based on a cross-solver predictor. This system adjusts its allocation using feedback from verification steps to guide solver selection. Experiments show BudgetPV requires less LLM generation computation than uniform allocation for the same tasks. The method demonstrates significant computation savings when incorporating cheaper solvers.
items.audio_script: From arXiv - cs.AI, "Budget-Aware Predict-and-Verify Theorem Proving with Heterogeneous LLM Solvers" details an agentic system for theorem proving that optimizes computation by managing heterogeneous large language model solvers. Experiments demonstrate that this system, BudgetPV, allocates computation across subgoals and different LLM solvers using a cross-solver predictor, adjusting allocation based on feedback from verification steps to guide solver selection. The methodology involves utilizing multiple theorem solvers with varying proving abilities and inference costs, and the system employs a predictor to manage the allocation. Results indicate that BudgetPV requires less LLM generation computation than uniform allocation for equivalent tasks and achieves significant computation savings through the incorporation of less computationally expensive solvers. This research suggests a pathway toward more efficient and cost-effective theorem proving in artificial intelligence systems.

items.title: NitroGen: Observations on the Action Dynamics, Visual Instruction Following, and Spatial Exploration
items.summary: NitroGen is an open vision-action foundation model designed for game control, trained via behavior cloning on gameplay videos. The research examines action adaptation, visual instruction following, and spatial exploration using frozen controllers in games like Hollow Knight and Trackmania. Results show NitroGen can adapt actions based on local context. However, it currently lacks the necessary planning, recovery, and exploration for longer-horizon game control. The work is categorized under Machine Learning.

items.title: TOUMAII: A 4.5M-Pair Tool-Calling Preference Dataset and Its Source-Agnostic Generator
items.summary: The research introduces TOUMAII, a large-scale dataset of 4.5 million tool-calling preference pairs derived from Agent-Ark/Toucan-1.5M conversations. This dataset is designed to address the scarcity of preference data for tool-calling, which is crucial for training models with direct preference optimization (DPO). The authors also release TOUMAII-Gen, a generator pipeline to create synthetic preference data reflecting model failures, ensuring source-agnostic training. Performance validation showed the DPO approach achieved parity with other high-quality datasets when fine-tuning a 3-billion-parameter model. The work provides code and datasets, emphasizing the importance of preference data for autonomous agent capabilities.

items.title: Learning under Bounded Manipulation for Quadratic Incentive Design
items.summary: The research studies a repeated quadratic incentive design game where a leader learns a follower's private type from noisy actions. The leader uses these estimates in an affine incentive rule, while the follower can manipulate observations to influence future estimates. A manipulation budget $C_T$, constraining the expected cumulative squared deviation from the myopic best response, is introduced. The paper establishes a minimax regret rate of order $\max\{\log T, \min\{C_T,T\}\}$ for approximately rational followers. Furthermore, increasing the follower's manipulation budget can unexpectedly reduce the leader's regret under a fixed learning rule.

items.title: Beyond Final Answers: Interpretable Tumor Immune Microenvironment Reasoning from H&E and mIF
items.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) struggle with reasoning about the tumor immune microenvironment (TIME) when relying solely on Hematoxylin and Eosin (H&E) stains. The study proposes HERMES, an R1-style MLLM that reasons jointly over paired H&E and multiplex immunofluorescence (mIF) data. HERMES is trained with a process reward that checks stated quantities against the ground truth provided by mIF, improving reasoning accuracy significantly. This method yields an 84.5% accuracy on colorectal cancer TIME tasks, outperforming other MLLMs. The integration of mIF provides the cell-level ground truth necessary to supervise the reasoning steps, leading to more verifiable and accurate conclusions.

items.title: Parasite Features: Causal Abstraction Through Spurious Pathways
items.summary: Causal Abstraction provides a framework for mechanistic interpretability by defining equivalence between neural networks and algorithms. The paper introduces the concept of "parasite features," which are spurious features that pass Causal Abstraction equivalence tests. These features arise when interpretability methods spuriously simulate the combined behavior of underlying feature directions. Experimentally, Distributed Alignment Search was shown to find parasite features using linear alignment maps in syntactic agreement and two-digit addition tasks. This work raises important considerations for the application of Causal Abstraction in mechanistic interpretability.

items.title: Cross-Attack Robust Aggregation for Federated Learning
items.summary: Federated learning models are vulnerable to poisoning attacks from compromised devices, which existing robust aggregation methods often fail to adequately address. FedTether is proposed as a method to enhance robustness by reweighting client updates based on their deviation from a coordinatewise median. This reweighting uses a robust, dead-zoned score applied during the server-side optimization step. Experiments show FedTether outperforms other methods by maintaining accuracy under various attack regimes, including stealthy and high-magnitude attacks. FedTether maintains strong performance even with partial participation without requiring shared data or validation sets.

items.title: Spectral Estimation with Deformed Decompression
items.summary: Sample covariance matrices contain valuable information encoded in their eigenvalues, but large-scale matrices pose computational challenges. Spectral decompression methods, such as spectral inversion and Free Decompression, exist but have limitations. Deformed Decompression (DD) is introduced as a novel framework for stably extrapolating spectral densities. DD uses properties of the companion matrix to frame the problem as a directed evolution of the Stieltjes transform. This approach offers a robust method for scaling covariance matrices, including those without unitary invariance, and successfully captures complex spectral signatures in experiments.

items.title: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens for Multimodal Retrieval and Generation
items.summary: Depth-Linked Residual Tokens (DepThink) is an efficient framework for multimodal retrieval and generation that addresses the latency of iterative architectures. It appends learnable residual tokens whose states are coupled via a lightweight, learnable residual recurrence within a single forward pass. This mechanism allows each token to capture complementary information missed by preceding tokens, proving expanded geometric directional reachability. Evaluation shows DepThink outperforms baselines and matches or exceeds looped architectures across various backbone sizes. Furthermore, it accelerates both training and inference compared to looped methods.

items.title: SDG: State-Dependent Gating at Chunk Boundaries for Linear Attention
items.summary: State-Dependent Gating (SDG) introduces element-wise gates based on the change in memory across chunk boundaries to provide state feedback. This method enables efficient chunkwise computation while maintaining parallel processing within each chunk. The approach addresses limitations in existing gated linear attention models by capturing state changes explicitly at chunk boundaries. Theoretical analysis confirms potential reconstruction benefits from this state-dependent gating under a signal-noise model. Empirical evaluations on large models show improvements across various language and reasoning tasks.

items.title: Language Diffusion Models are Associative Memories Capable of Retrieving Unseen Data
items.summary: Language diffusion models, specifically Uniform-based Discrete Diffusion Models (UDDMs), exhibit behavior consistent with Associative Memories (AMs) possessing emergent creative capabilities. This is explored by examining how these models memorize training data and generalize to unseen data. A transition from memorization to generalization can be quantitatively detected by analyzing the conditional entropy of predicted token sequences. Memorization is indicated by vanishing conditional entropy, while generalization involves a finite conditional entropy across most tokens. Therefore, conditional entropy provides a method to probe the memorization-to-generalization boundary in deployed models.

items.title: Budgeted Subset Selection with a Transferable Learned Value Model
items.summary: A framework called SALVES is introduced for budgeted subset selection by decomposing the problem into value estimation and search. It trains a value model using supervised learning on tasks where hidden information is known to predict candidate utility on new tasks. Selection is then performed by choosing subsets from these predictions, typically using simulated annealing with a redundancy penalty. The learned value model is transferable across new classes, pretrained networks, datasets, and data types. SALVES successfully matches or outperforms application-specific baselines across four applications, often requiring fewer bands for equal accuracy.

items.title: Coherence by Construction: Synthesizing CTI Knowledge Graphs and the Formal Limits of Coherence Validation
items.summary: The study proposes a generation by simulation paradigm for knowledge graphs, focusing on constructing coherence through a causal process rather than describing the artifact directly. Language model agents propose intents, and a deterministic referee validates outcomes against an explicit world model, ensuring relations are emitted only when represented events occur. The framework is applied to cyber threat intelligence knowledge graphs using methods like evolutionary genetic operators on graph genomes. The research proves that a validator cannot determine coherence simply by checking if a generated graph matches a random graph structure. Ultimately, the work cautions that structural validation alone is uninformative for coherence in construction-based knowledge synthesis.

items.title: Can pretrained Transformers deliver semiparametrically efficient inference?
items.summary: A single pretrained Transformer can provide efficient estimation and valid inference for a family of estimands in one forward pass. This is achieved by learning the posterior mean and covariance from pretraining data, without needing to derive influence functions or estimate nuisance functions. The method ensures that the posterior mean is efficient for queried estimands under specific pretraining conditions. Experiments in causal inference, partial linear regression, and survival analysis show the Transformer achieves low estimation error with fast computation. The results suggest that pretrained Transformers can deliver semiparametrically efficient inference.

items.title: On the loss landscape of the linear neural network: beyond critical points
items.summary: The paper addresses the lack of a global description for the loss landscape of linear neural networks beyond their critical points. It introduces a new structure called the critical thalweg, which encompasses all critical points and possesses specific geometric properties. This framework provides a global view of the loss landscape that is easily visualized in two dimensions. The work offers a geometric proof of existing results using simpler assumptions and suggests that gradient descent is attracted towards this thalweg. Empirical evidence indicates that gradient descent follows this path to reach the global minimum.

items.title: Semiparametric Efficiency for Entropic Optimal Transport under Structured Distribution Shift
items.summary: The study investigates the semiparametric efficiency of entropic optimal transport (EOT) when structured distribution shifts occur. It examines whether structural information can improve the estimation of EOT and quantifies the variance gain from restrictions under specific conditions. The work involves a fixed-dimensional exponential density ratio model with a nonparametric baseline and a fixed positive regularization. The analysis shows that the variance gain can be zero and depends on the behavior of the tilt space as samples grow. Finally, the study explores phase transitions in the limiting distribution based on the balance of source fluctuations and quadratic tilt errors.

items.title: Optimal Linear Regression Without a Variance
items.summary: The study examines high-probability linear regression in a regime where regression noise has a finite conditional $\alpha$-moment $\nu$. A black-box reduction is provided to convert finite-variance regression procedures into weak-moment procedures via empirical residual pruning. Under a finite fourth-moment condition on covariates, a finite-variance subroutine achieving the sub-Gaussian rate yields a specific error bound dependent on the sample size. This result includes a matching minimax lower bound, and the reduction is computationally efficient. Furthermore, the work provides distribution-free prediction guarantees and an analogous $\alpha$-agnostic reduction for mean estimation.

items.title: Memorization and Generalization in Generative Models: A Perspective From Energy-based Modeling and Associative Memory
items.summary: The research explores the coexistence of memorization and generalization in generative models by framing them through Associative Memory (AM) principles. It posits that memorization and generalization can stem from a single retrieval process based on basins of attraction. Diffusion models are shown to behave as AMs, exhibiting spurious states that indicate nascent generative capability. Uniform-state discrete diffusion models also function as AMs, where expanding basins for unseen examples demonstrate generalization. Ultimately, AM provides a framework for understanding when a generative model recalls versus when it creates.

items.title: Realistic Robustness Evaluation of Tabular Data Driven Models
items.summary: The study addresses the limited research on adversarial robustness in tabular data, which is widely used in real-world systems. It introduces AURORA, a modular, open-source tool designed to evaluate the robustness of machine learning models on tabular data classification. AURORA integrates various adversarial perturbation methods and evaluation metrics into a unified framework for systematic assessment. The tool's evaluation report quantifies performance degradation and identifies model vulnerabilities while incorporating a distance adjustment mechanism for realistic perturbations. This approach provides a more reliable assessment of model robustness in tabular data.

items.title: ChatAtom: A Multi-Agent LLM System for Molecular Dynamics Simulation and Visualization
items.summary: ChatAtom is a multi-agent Large Language Model system designed to automate molecular dynamics (MD) simulation workflows. It translates natural language requests into complete MD workflows, eliminating the need for users to write input scripts or analysis code. Agents like an orchestrator, LAMMPS, and OVITO, along with a HPC agent, manage the process using generator-reviewer pairs for script preparation. The system features a browser interface for streaming simulation data and supports loadable skills for autonomous hypothesis testing. This system aims to lower the barrier to conducting MD studies by integrating script generation, execution, visualization, and analysis into one observable pipeline.
